question: Order ORD-023 was split into two shipments. Give me the status of each and explain why it was split.
agent_answer:
Here's the full picture for ORD-023 (OMS: status **shipped**, priority **urgent**, customer CUST-004 / Mandarin Oriental):

## Shipments

| | SHP-017 | SHP-018 |
|---|---|---|
| **Status** | in_transit | in_transit |
| **Carrier** | SCG Cold Chain (CAR-002) | Kerry Express (CAR-001) |
| **Carrier type** | Refrigerated | Ground |
| **Product** | PROD-001 — Nam Doc Mai Mango Box 5kg | PROD-006 — Dried Mango Slices 500g |
| **Tracking** | SCG-20260212-017A | KRY-20260212-017B |
| **Dispatched** | 2026-02-12 08:00 | 2026-02-12 08:00 |
| **ETA** | 2026-02-13 17:00 | 2026-02-14 17:00 |

*Source: TMS*

## Why it was split

The two line items require incompatible carrier types (WMS):

- **PROD-001** (Nam Doc Mai fresh mango, shelf life 7 days) has `storage_type: refrigerated` → **must** use a cold chain carrier
- **PROD-006** (Dried Mango Slices, shelf life 180 days) has `storage_type: ambient` → can use a cheaper ground carrier

Shipping them together on a single carrier would either spoil the fresh mangoes (ground truck) or unnecessarily increase cost (cold chain for dried goods). The split is the correct call per the refrigerated-carrier business rule.

**Note:** SHP-017 (fresh mangoes) arrives Feb 13, SHP-018 (dried) arrives Feb 14 — the urgent required date is Feb 15, so both are on track.
